classification.difficultyReason: Translate labelled boxes into multiples of b and loose apples into constants, preserving the pictured operations and equality, including b on both sides.

content.prompt: $b$ represents the number of apples in each box. Write an equation for each scenario.

spec.description: Two boxes labelled b, plus six apples in two rows of three, equals ten apples in two rows of five.
spec.answerVisibility: Object counts, box labels and operation symbols are permanent givens. The supplied blue equation is stored separately as the answer.

answer.worked: Two boxes contain $2b$ apples. Adding the six loose apples gives ten apples: $$2b+6=10.$$

spec.description: One box labelled b, minus three apples arranged as one above two, equals two vertically stacked apples.
spec.mathematics: b - 3 = 2; the box represents b apples.
spec.answerVisibility: Object counts, the box label and operation symbols are permanent givens. The supplied blue equation is stored separately as the answer.

answer.worked: Removing three apples from the $b$ apples in one box leaves two: $$b-3=2.$$

spec.description: Three boxes labelled b, plus four apples in two rows of two, equals seven apples arranged as three above four.
spec.answerVisibility: Object counts, box labels and operation symbols are permanent givens. The supplied blue equation is stored separately as the answer.

answer.worked: Three boxes contain $3b$ apples. Adding the four loose apples gives seven apples: $$3b+4=7.$$

spec.description: Two boxes labelled b, minus two vertically stacked apples, equals one box labelled b.
spec.mathematics: 2b - 2 = b; every box represents the same number b of apples.
spec.answerVisibility: All three variable-labelled boxes, the two apples and operation symbols are permanent givens. The supplied blue equation is stored separately as the answer.

answer.worked: Two boxes contain $2b$ apples. Removing two apples leaves the number in one box: $$2b-2=b.$$
